correctness.rationale: After isometric normalization to \(F(z)=(z,A z^2)\), the exact normal projection of a chord gives a universal lower bound \(r\ge 1/(2A)\) for any point having two nearest graph points. Closedness and properness guarantee existence of nearest points, hence uniqueness below this radius. The axis points \(y_v=(0,v)\), \(v>1/(2A)\), have two explicit global nearest points with common distance decreasing to \(1/(2A)\), proving the matching upper bound.

originality.rationale: The recent primary article proves qualitative uniform flatness of all polynomial graphs. Its accessible material does not state an exact radius, and source-specific searches found no quadratic reach formula. The classic Bargmann--Fock papers define and use tubular uniform flatness rather than computing this invariant for quadratic graphs. The complete lead article was not accessible, so possible internal overlap is retained as a residual risk rather than treated as disproved.

value.rationale: The lead theorem creates a natural new uniformly flat class but leaves the tube scale qualitative. Degree two is the first nonlinear case, and reach is precisely the canonical invariant measuring the largest collision-free nearest-point tube. The accepted result gives a complete exact classification for that degree, proves lower-order coefficients are irrelevant, and supplies a sharp quantitative benchmark for future interpolation estimates and higher-degree reach questions.
